LANDING PR for story #726: recipes, a shelf spelled through '..' beneath an absent component refuses, the personal install leaves nothing behind, contributing's `recipes list` is hermetic, and a personal install refuses a name the project shelf holds (#697 slice A's follow-ups). Operator, 2026-10-17, on PR #722 (recorded on #697), ruling 6, verbatim: "The LOW, a `..` beneath a component that doesn't exist reading as an empty shelf (in both directions), is accepted. Its fix is filed as #726, with the slice's other follow-ups."

Read issue #726 whole first: its Acceptance is what done means.

The branch story-726-shelf-spellings ends at 70f5760f, cut from main 7ed4acc6 (story run implement-story-726-recipes-a-sh-658b341e). It has two commits, 9 files:
- 0fcfcafd, all four items:
  1. `resolving` calls a new `climbs`. Where the part of the shelf beneath its nearest standing entry holds a `..`, it refuses with Unshelved::Climbing {origin, shelf, at}. ASSUMPTION: a relative shelf with no standing ancestor is judged beneath the current directory (at='.'). A `..` beneath a standing entry still resolves. recipes list and doctor keep their existing warning lines ('warning: recipes dir <shelf>: No such file or directory (os error 2)' and 'warn     personal shelf: ...'); doctor's exit stays healthy.
  2. Made::above builds its guard first, then makes each directory outermost-first and records each once made. A failure is Unshelved::Unmade {shelf, at, cause}. An entry whose presence cannot be read no longer counts as standing.
  3. contributing.rs's `recipes list` runs under doc_samples::hermetic (made pub(crate)), shared rather than copied.
  4. A Shadowing refusal for a name the project shelf holds, with a `stands` helper factored out of holding_in. ASSUMPTION: in a library or bare layout the project shelf is `recipes` relative to the current directory, as --recipe resolves it.
  - Decision 0083 gains a proposed "Extension, 2026-10-17: the shelf follow-ups (#726)" at the end of the #697 addendum, with the three texts byte for byte.
- 70f5760f, answering the review's MEDIUM: recipes.rs's `planned` also installs every extends base the personal shelf lacks, so a base the project shelf held was installed and later refused as Shadowed.
  - The install's shelf parameter is now `Onto<'_>` (Project | Personal { project }) in recipes/personal.rs, replacing Origin in recipes::add and install_held.
  - `Onto::unshadowing(&planned, dir)` runs in install_held right after `planned`, before refuse_within and any copy, and judges every planned name. The leaf-only check is gone.
  - Consequence: a shadowed leaf now refuses after the source is fetched (a URL source is cloned first), with the same text and nothing left behind.
  - recipes.rs is at 787 of its 800-line cap; personal.rs is at 482.
- The final review ruled residual LOW. Its one finding (decision 0071 ruling 8): personal.rs:322-325, holding_in returns the project shelf BEFORE its resolving call when no personal shelf is placed (XDG_CONFIG_HOME and HOME unset or relative). So on the project origin the Climbing refusal fires only when a personal shelf is placed. `env -u XDG_CONFIG_HOME -u HOME brokkr recipes show x --dir .brokkr/recipes/sub/..` printed "recipe 'x' not found under ..." instead. It fails closed, but decision 0083's proposed extension says the refusal fires "on either origin, every verb ruling 2 names", which over-claims.
  - The chief's notes: the read surfaces show a climbing shelf by the existing warning lines, not Climbing's text; a climbing() expected-text helper exists once per test layer (jscpd holds).
  - Follow-ups named: personal::add judges the personal shelf twice (head, and super::add's place); removing the second needs recipes.rs.
- Host exact coverage on 70f5760f is 100% (60960/60960 lines, 8028/8028 branches, 7698/7698 functions). Host lints hold. The branch merges clean with main 24cdf3b2.

THE IMPLEMENT PHASE FIXES THE CARRIED LOW FIRST: hoist `resolving(Origin::Project, &project)?` above the `let Some(personal) = personal else` early return in holding_in, so the project origin's Climbing refusal fires with or without a personal shelf. Bind it through the binary with XDG_CONFIG_HOME and HOME removed from the child's environment (Command::env_remove, not a shell prefix), expecting the exact Climbing text on recipes show --dir and run --recipes-dir, plus a removal control. If hoisting changes any other observable refusal or order, stop and narrow the decision sentence instead, and say which you did.

Every review position, panel member or chief, is READ-ONLY: it changes no tracked file and makes no commit, whatever this text asks below. It reports each finding. Only the implement phase fixes a finding the review returns.

Judge, on the HEAD binary and tests:
1. #726's Acceptance, item by item:
   - Climbing on both origins, on every verb ruling 2 names, with and without a personal shelf placed;
   - a `..` beneath a standing entry is unchanged;
   - Made::above leaves the temporary tree byte-identical after a failure at any depth, and Unmade names the shelf;
   - contributing's `recipes list` is hermetic through the shared helper;
   - Shadowing judges every name the install would copy (leaf and every extends base), before any copy, and an unreadable project shelf refuses as Unread.
2. Order: personal::add's and install_held's refusal order. Name every refusal whose position moved against main (the shadowed leaf now refusing after the fetch), and say whether any first refusal for a multi-defect install changed.
3. Decision 0083's proposed #726 extension: Status proposed; every sentence true of HEAD (especially "on either origin"); the three texts (Climbing, Unmade, Shadowing) byte for byte as the binary prints them.
4. The two ASSUMPTIONS (a relative shelf with no standing ancestor judged beneath '.'; the project shelf in a library or bare layout is `recipes` relative to the current directory): say whether each is what --recipe and `recipes list` already do, and state each as an operator ruling.
5. Scope: only recipes.rs, recipes/personal.rs, personal_tests.rs, recipes/tests.rs, verbs/setup.rs, tests/shelf.rs, tests/contributing.rs, tests/doc_samples.rs and decision 0083 (plus what the LOW's fix adds); no brokkr-runtime, places.rs, doctor*, cli_args.rs, engine*, bundle*, adapters*, contracts/, fixtures/, policy/phase-machine.json or reference/ change. recipes.rs stays at 800 lines or under.
6. For the PR, list the rulings the operator must make:
   - the three refusal texts;
   - the 0083 extension;
   - the two assumptions;
   - the read surfaces keeping their warning lines rather than Climbing's text;
   - the shadowed leaf refusing after the fetch.
   Name the follow-ups (the double personal-shelf judgement in recipes.rs; the climbing() helper per layer).

This run lands one pull request under decision 0051, so the contribution gate can vouch for it.

For the implement phase only: fix the carried LOW as above; if a finding returns the branch, fix exactly that finding and prove it with a test bound by a compiling mutation. Then run, all clean: cargo fmt --all -- --check; cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings; cargo test -p brokkr-cli --lib --locked -- recipes::; cargo test -p brokkr-cli --test it --locked -- shelf:: recipes:: contributing:: doc_samples:: doc_truth:: init_stacks:: suppressions:: house_prose:: decisions_index::; typos --hidden; quality/ratchet.sh files, clones and api; `cargo crap --path crates/brokkr-cli/src --format json` for every function you add or change; git diff --check. A new test file is named *_tests.rs.

Other work runs in parallel: decision 0065 slice two (the-forge-b9; NEVER message it, or any brokkr-wt-* seat) runs U8a2a on brokkr-runtime engine.rs, engine/broker.rs (and new children beside it), engine/dispatch.rs, engine/panel.rs and engine/sequence.rs, then U8a2b on engine/broker.rs and engine.rs; it owns cli_args.rs, doctor.rs and doctor/capabilities.rs. #735 (recipes add's destination links, the #703 follow-ups) waits for this branch to merge. This landing touches none of their files.

Commit one signed-off commit ending "Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>", and never push. Do not run scripts/coverage-exact.sh; the controller runs it. Run every command in the foreground: never background a command or schedule a wakeup, because a headless seat ends when it waits.

Threat model (operator ruling, 2026-09-26): catch realistic accidental misuse, and fail closed on what cannot be read.

# OpenSpec analyze

Judge duplication, ambiguity, underspecification, house alignment, coverage gaps, and inconsistency across proposal, deltas, design and tasks. Treat the realm house as the constitution. Return each finding with severity and its earliest owning artifact; zero findings is consistent.
instructions.clarify:
# OpenSpec clarify

Judge underspecified areas, unquantified language, missing decisions, capability/delta mismatches, and requirements without adequate scenarios. Return every ambiguity with the evidence needed to settle it; zero findings is clear.
instructions.design:
# OpenSpec design

Write `openspec/changes/<change>/design.md`. Record context, goals and non-goals, decisions with alternatives, risks, migration, and open questions. On return, revise the design and dependent artifacts so no finding is merely acknowledged.

# OpenSpec return

Revise the returned change in dependency order. Encode an answered ambiguity as a scenario, record design choices under `## Decisions`, and keep every dependent artifact coherent. Record a reasoned refusal in the owning artifact.
instructions.implement:
# OpenSpec tasks

Write `openspec/changes/<change>/tasks.md` as numbered groups of checkboxes. Name the requirement served by every task. On return, repair the breakdown and its requirement coverage before implementation resumes.

# OpenSpec return

Revise the returned change in dependency order. Encode an answered ambiguity as a scenario, record design choices under `## Decisions`, and keep every dependent artifact coherent. Record a reasoned refusal in the owning artifact.

Change location: `openspec/changes/{change}`. Archive operation: ["openspec","archive","{change}","--yes"].

# OpenSpec archive

Folding a change is the last task: run the archive operation named above,
which moves the change directory under `openspec/changes/archive/` and
folds its deltas into `openspec/specs/`. Folding also records which change
wrote which capability, so every capability the change touched carries a
`## Provenance` list.

After the archive operation, open each capability's
`openspec/specs/<capability>/spec.md` that the change touched and append
exactly one line under a `## Provenance` heading held at the end of the
file:

`- \`<archived-directory-name>\` — folded <YYYY-MM-DD>`

`<archived-directory-name>` is the directory the archive operation
created under `openspec/changes/archive/`; `<YYYY-MM-DD>` is the day it
was folded. Append only: never rewrite, reorder or remove an existing
provenance line, because standing truth accumulates and is not edited into
a different meaning. The line is a pointer, not a summary — it names the
change and nothing else, and the why stays in the change directory.

house.content:
This realm is a Rust workspace. Production code is Rust under `crates/`; the
Rust-only architecture is recorded by decision 0009. Semantic changes carry a
decision document with status `proposed` because only the operator accepts one.
Intake seats read `README.md` and decisions 0004 and 0005 before framing a
commission, along with the code and history it touches.

The frozen v1 contracts under `contracts/`, the production table at
`policy/phase-machine.json`, and `reference/` (its schemas included) are
read-only.
A contract change lands as a new version file beside the old one, never as an
edit. The evaluator corpus under `fixtures/` is also frozen and is never
regenerated, only versioned.

Tests are part of every change. Extend the suite that proves the code, run
`cargo test --workspace`, compile `recipes/self`, and leave formatting, clippy,
and the exact-coverage gate clean before reporting success.

Commit completed work with `git` using the repository's message style. Never
push.

The supported hosts are Linux and macOS (decision 0063); WSL2 is Linux. Write
no Windows-conditional code, test or evidence.

## Architecture

Decision 0071 rules how code here is shaped. Build to it, and cite its ruling
numbers in what you judge. Where a gate named below holds a rule, the gate is
the authority, and a finding it would catch is the gate's.

- **Pure core (ruling 1).** `brokkr-core` and `brokkr-view` do no I/O and read
  no clock, environment or randomness. They run no process. Pass `now`, paths
  and environment in as arguments. Effects live in the crates above core and
  view, and are journaled.
- **Enums and data, not traits (ruling 2).** A closed set is an enum matched
  exhaustively, with no wildcard arm that decides behaviour. Anything an
  operator extends is data under `adapters/`, `agents/`, `recipes/` or
  `realms.json`, validated and digested. Add a trait only for a seam whose
  contract spans several operations that must stay consistent with one
  another, reached across a process or service boundary, and name that seam
  in its doc comment. `ProducerTransport` is the one such trait today. A test
  double alone does not make a seam: a single substitutable function is a
  closure seam (`*_with`, `*_in`), which is how the house inverts a
  dependency otherwise.
- **Typed at the edge (ruling 3).** Parse wire, file and harness data once
  into a type, with `serde` and `deny_unknown_fields` where the contract is
  closed. `serde_json::Value` never goes past the edge, into state, or back
  out by string key. Never put `format!("{:?}")` in anything digested or
  journaled. A doubly-optional field or a string vocabulary is a missing enum.
- **Small functions (ruling 4).** New and changed functions stay within 100
  lines, nesting depth 5 and 7 parameters. Cyclomatic complexity follows
  the operator's 2026-09-26 ruling: a function may reach the higher of 15
  and its baseline, so a new function stays within 15, an existing one may
  change freely up to 15, and one already over 15 may only shrink.
  Production files stay within 800 lines and test files within 2,000, and a
  file already over may not grow. Add no new `jscpd` clone in production
  code, test code or data. `quality/` holds the measured baseline. Today's
  offenders carry `#[allow(clippy::…)]`, and #337 converts them to
  `#[expect(clippy::…, reason = "…")]`. Add a suppression only by a ruling,
  and remove it when you fix the function. A new suppression is
  `#[expect(…, reason)]`, never `#[allow]`.
- **Once (ruling 5).** Every fact has one home. A repeated vocabulary, skeleton
  or helper becomes one function or one table. An agent is defined once under
  `agents/`, and seats hire it by reference. A recipe that differs from another
  by a model, a seat or an entry is an `extends` overlay, never a copy. The
  agent library does not yet accept `extends`, and #360 builds it. Until then,
  a variation of an agent lives at the seat that hires it, overridden in a
  recipe overlay. It is never a second agent file that restates the first. A
  copy that must exist, such as a script a bundle pins, is held to its source
  by a test.
- **Nothing unused (ruling 6).** Add no alias, agent, contract version, flag or
  `pub` item without a consumer, and prefer `pub(crate)`. A deprecation names
  the release that removes it.
- **One derivation (ruling 7).** A fact shown on two surfaces is derived once
  in `brokkr-view`. The CLI, the TUI and `ui.html` only paint it. The engine
  never admits anything by a display-crate function.
- **Typed errors (ruling 8).** Return a `thiserror` enum whose `Display` keeps
  the operator's text. Tests match variants and pin each module's text once.
  Add no new `Result<_, String>`.
- **Tests that bind (ruling 9).** Assert exact values or variants, never
  `is_err()` alone. Show that every new test binds: a compiling mutation that
  removes the behaviour must make it fail. Restore the behaviour and record
  the failing test. Share fixtures through builders. Never change the process
  environment without a guard that restores it on unwind. A production guard
  left out because the exact-coverage gate would count it unreachable carries
  a removal-control test for the invariant that makes it unreachable, and the
  comment explaining the omission names that test.
- **The house's patterns (ruling 10).**
  - A harness is a module behind `AdapterKind`. This is the target form;
    today all five kinds share one module, and #347 and #348 build the
    split.
  - A CLI verb is a `Cmd` variant plus a handler.
  - A long parameter list becomes a parameter object.
  - Argv and mount tables are built with a builder.
  - Observing the world is split from deciding on it.
  - Never use a trait-object registry for a closed set.

Judges rate a finding against these rulings by this table, and cite the ruling
number:

- **info:** something a house gate would catch. The gate's verdict is the
  authority.
- **low:** a new or changed function over a ceiling, a rule written a second
  time, an item added without a consumer, or a `Value` carried past its edge
  within one module.
- **medium:** an untyped vocabulary that crosses crates, recipe or agent data
  copied instead of extended, a fact derived a second time on another surface,
  an error matched by its text, or a new test that cannot fail.
- **high or above:** any violation that hides a fail-open path or weakens a
  refusal. It is carried as a security finding.

A principle the implementer bent knowingly, and named with its reason in
`notes`, is still rated, and the judge carries that reason with the finding.

## Release configuration

The release manager prepares the candidate and profile patches; the operator
publishes them. Local validation is preparation work. Remote CI on the final PR
head, publication, channel updates and live-profile verification are handoff
steps, recorded as pending until their remote results exist. Historical
"live from" channel versions and old journal examples are historical facts,
not current-version references to replace.

With XDG_CONFIG_HOME and HOME removed from the child environment, recipes/sub absent, `brokkr recipes show x --dir recipes/sub/..` exits 1 with exactly `error: recipe 'x' not found under recipes/sub/..; install it with `brokkr recipes add <source> --name x`` (then newline), rather than Climbing. `run --recipe x --recipes-dir recipes/sub/.. --feature review --no-view` likewise emits not-found. Setting XDG_CONFIG_HOME to an absolute absent directory makes both emit the required Climbing text beneath recipes. Nothing runs: diagnostic gap, no security residual. The required landing correction and its env_remove binary regression/removal control are absent. Decision 0083:1060 still overclaims 'on either origin, every verb'. Remediation constraint: the unconditional hoist also changes an existing non-climbing refusal: with both variables removed, `recipes show x --dir Cargo.toml` currently emits not-found, whereas the resolving path with a personal placement emits Unread/not a directory. Therefore honor the commission's stop-and-narrow fallback if that unrelated diagnostic change is forbidden; this review changed neither code nor decision.

Acceptance: item 1 holds with personal placement on all five project read verbs and on the shared personal read route, but fails the no-personal-placement requirement above. A standing component's '..' still resolves normally (exact resolved-place unit assertion). Item 2: Made builds its guard before creation, creates outermost-first, records each success, and removes deepest-first on error; the 256-byte component unit and binary tests pass, asserting Unmade's exact shelf/directory text and empty temporary tree/repository unchanged. Item 3 shares doc_samples::hermetic, setting a fresh absolute XDG_CONFIG_HOME; no helper copy. Item 4 judges leaf and every planned extends base with resolving/stands before any copy; leaf/base Shadowing binary tests and dangling-project-shelf Unread unit test pass. No further concrete failure found.

Refusal order: HEAD personal::add is shelf placement -> personal resolving -> Made::above -> super::add (Unplain::Name -> Source::judge's Unplain::Path/AtPath::Local -> personal place/resolving -> World discovery -> destination-exists -> fetch) -> Shelf::make -> planned -> project resolving/stands/Shadowing -> Within -> FolderBundle -> Places/agent planning -> copy -> compile Refused. Against main, the existing personal Unread judgement moves ahead of Made and name/source validation; for example, an unreadable shelf entry with an otherwise standing parent plus invalid --name now reports Unread before Unplain::Name. Creation errors become typed Unmade, and Climbing is a new earlier refusal. Project Unread/Unreadable and Shadowing newly precede Within, FolderBundle, agent planning errors, copy failures and compile Refused, so multi-defect first refusals can change. Against 0fcfcafd specifically, shadowed-leaf refusal moved after fetch (including URL clone), Shelf::make and planning; a bad fetch/planning error now wins over that clash. Relative order among the remaining checks is unchanged; all guards unwind before returning.
